A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SemCSE-Multi work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite added subsections and repagination.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval, similarity-correlation, and embedding-decoding experiments in invasion biology, with additional medical-domain experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, generated-text evaluation, and permutation-test results.

M1.justification: The proposed aspect-specific contrastive training, L2 distillation, frozen-LLM decoding, and t-SNE reconstruction procedures remain unchanged. Removing 'v2' from the SciDeBERTa name does not establish an encoder change. The newly evaluated directly trained unified model is a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same invasion-biology corpus and six aspects, and the same PubMed collection and three medical aspects. The added evaluations use existing coverage; the medical experiments were already present in v1's Appendix B.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds base SciDeBERTa to the summary-retrieval comparison. New Appendix A.7 evaluates a directly trained unified model against the proposed two-stage approach. Existing comparator sets in Table 2 and the medical experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Decoder evaluation adds SciBERT-based BERTScore alongside perplexity, with Table 3 reporting matching, reconstructed, and shuffled conditions. Appendix A.7 introduces joint contrastive training for the new baseline. Existing splits, sample sizes, model sizes, and stated training hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.7 directly tests whether separate aspect-model training followed by distillation improves disentanglement compared with joint training. This adds a targeted architectural ablation; existing cross-aspect retrieval, decoder controls, and medical top-10 retrieval analysis remain.

E5.justification: V1 provides no corresponding significance analysis. New Appendix A.6 introduces systematic testing of matching versus nonmatching aspect correlations using 10,000 permutations per comparison, with explicit exceptions for recommendation and hypothesis embeddings evaluated against research-question targets. This adds statistical support for a central empirical claim.

E6.justification: Existing table values are retained. Additions include SciDeBERTa retrieval scores and BERTScores: Llama's general-hypothesis scores are 77.5 for matching and 71.9 for shuffled inputs. Appendix A.7 reports selected off-diagonal means of 21.43 for SemCSE-Multi versus 28.3 for the direct baseline, with similar diagonal means of 42.6 versus 42.8.

T1.justification: The contrastive objective, aspect-weighted distance, t-SNE equations, and PCA-constrained reconstruction mathematics are unchanged, including the renumbered appendices. No theoretical results or proofs are added; the new permutation procedure concerns statistical evaluation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: controllable aspect-specific embeddings, a unified distilled encoder, and decoding of embeddings and unoccupied visualization regions. Added experiments support these contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3 and A.7 add a co-adaptation explanation for information leaking between jointly trained aspects. Appendix A.1 clarifies expert usefulness and availability in abstracts as aspect-selection criteria. The decoding discussion distinguishes reference likelihood from generated-text alignment; the existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 documents separate aspect batches and summary-summary plus abstract-summary matching for the new baseline. Section 5.2 identifies SciBERT as the BERTScore backbone. Existing training details, decoder implementation, and code/checkpoint access information are preserved.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to BERTScore and SciBERT. Section 4.3 also explains why other multifaceted models are excluded from comparison, citing their need for supervised data for freely selected aspects. The broader related-work positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 consolidates the former Motivation subsection into the introduction, condenses several explanatory passages, and adds two appendix subsections with corresponding renumbering. Incorrect references to the medical experiments as Appendix A.8 are corrected to Appendix B. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a comparator row, and Table 3 expands into separate perplexity and BERTScore blocks with an updated caption. Existing figures and appendix tables retain their content and visual design, with some relocated through page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through BERTScore on actual generations (Table 3), a direct test of two-stage training (Appendix A.7), and explicit significance reporting with exceptions (Appendix A.6). These address gaps in v1's support for decoding and disentanglement. The gains remain incremental because the datasets, prior results, and substantial reliance on LLM-generated references are unchanged.
